subtopics.title: VAT: the Fifteen Percent on Almost Everything

questions.question: A kettle priced at R360 excluding VAT sells, with VAT at 15%, for:
To remove VAT from a VAT-inclusive price of R414, the correct move is:
Taking 15% off R414 instead of dividing by 1,15 gives R351,90, which is wrong because:
options: It takes 15% of the larger, already-taxed figure
VAT can never be removed from a price

questions.question: Which list contains only zero-rated items?
options: Brown bread, rice, fresh fruit, eggs, milk

subtopics.title: UIF: One Percent from Each Side

questions.question: The UIF deduction on a gross salary of R9 200 is:
The total that reaches the fund each month for that worker is:
options: R184 — 1% from the worker and 1% from the employer

questions.question: UIF is calculated on:
options: The total of the other deductions

questions.question: With gross pay of R9 200, UIF of R92 and other deductions of R648, net pay is:

subtopics.title: Exchange Rates: the Price of the Rand

questions.question: At R19,80 per euro, an online course billed at €150 costs:
At the same rate, R6 000 converts to:
If the rate moves from R19,80 to R20,60 per euro, the rand has:
options: Strengthened, because the number went up
Weakened — each euro now costs more rand

questions.question: A weaker rand is GOOD news for:
options: A family filling up with petrol
A student paying a course fee in euros
A family receiving €250 from a relative in Dublin

subtopics.title: Tariff Systems: Which Option Is Cheaper for You

questions.question: Option P charges R120 per month plus R0,60 per minute. Its cost formula is:
At 250 minutes, Option P (R120 + R0,60/min) against Option Q (R1,40/min) gives:
options: P: R270, Q: R350 — Q wins
P: R270, Q: R350 — P wins
P: R180, Q: R140 — Q wins
P: R350, Q: R270 — Q wins

questions.question: The crossing point of the two options is found by:
options: Choosing the option with the smaller monthly charge
Setting 120 + 0,60 × m equal to 1,40 × m, giving 150 minutes

questions.question: On a graph of the two options, the break-even point of the comparison appears as:
options: The steepest section of either line
The point where Option Q crosses the vertical axis
The point where Option P starts
The point where the two cost lines intersect

subtopics.title: The Tax Inside the Till Slip

questions.question: The one-move shortcut for adding 15% VAT to a price is:
Adding 15% to a price and then taking 15% off the result:
options: Returns you exactly to the original price
Never brings you home, because the second 15% is measured on a bigger number

questions.question: On a till slip mixing taxable and zero-rated items, VAT is calculated:
options: Only on the taxable lines, leaving the protected basket untouched

subtopics.title: The Two R92s on the Payslip

questions.question: The no-calculator way to find 1% of a gross salary is to:
options: Slide the decimal comma two places — R9 200 becomes R92

questions.question: Asked 'how much does the worker contribute to UIF?' when gross pay is R9 200, the answer is:
options: R92 — the employer's R92 never appears on the payslip

questions.question: The payslip identity that always holds is:
UIF exists so that:
options: The government collects VAT on wages
Workers pay for their own pensions
A retrenched worker receives a temporary income while looking for work

subtopics.title: Rands Abroad and the Cheaper Phone Deal

questions.question: Thinking of a euro as an item priced at R19,80, converting R6 000 into euros means:
options: Asking how many R19,80 items the money buys — divide, about €303

questions.question: When the rand weakens, the aunt's €250 sent home from Dublin:
options: Becomes more rand — painful at the petrol pump, welcome for the receiving family
Stays exactly the same in rand

questions.question: The general rule for tariff comparisons is:
options: The option with no monthly charge is always cheaper
The option with the fixed charge is always cheaper
Fixed-charge options suit heavy users; pay-as-you-go suits light users; they trade places at the break-even point
Both options always cost the same at 100 minutes

questions.question: The best final answer to a two-option tariff question is:
options: At 100 minutes a month, take Q and keep R40
